meta.description: You describe your rooms, teachers, groups and rules. Planner places the sessions, and tells you why when it cannot.

entete.accroche: You describe your rooms, teachers, groups and rules. Planner places the sessions, and tells you why when it cannot.

cartes.texte: School leaders and the registrar's office find rooms, exams and timetable figures in one place.
Attendance, quizzes, games and polls all happen in the same tool, with the same account.
Two-factor authentication, role-based access, a security log, properly closed accounts, AI without student data.

lignes.avant: Rooms, teachers and groups are assigned by hand.
lignes.avec: You describe your rooms, teachers, groups and rules. Planner places the sessions, and tells you why when it cannot.

lignes.avant: Account lists move around in files that get typed in again.
lignes.avec: Teachers, students, programmes, groups and courses import from a CSV file.

lignes.avant: A postponement is confirmed through messages.
lignes.avec: The teacher asks, the registrar approves, and the students concerned are notified.

lignes.avant: The grid goes to teachers as an attachment.
lignes.avec: The timetable exports as a PDF, on the school's own time-slot grid.

lignes.avant: Each version of the grid is another file.
lignes.avec: Every calculation is kept. You go back to an earlier version whenever you want.

questions.question: Can lists be imported?
questions.reponse: The administration can import lists of accounts, students and teachers from compatible CSV files.

questions.question: How is a refused session explained?
questions.reponse: When a session cannot be placed, Planner names the rule that blocks it, or what is missing: a slot, a room, a teacher.

questions.question: Who tells students about a postponement?
questions.reponse: The teacher asks, the registrar approves, and the students concerned are notified.
